reviews.title: A Pay-to-Play App That Can Punish You for Actually Using It
reviews.text:
If you’re considering this app, especially as a man, here’s what you should know before spending your hard-earned money.

1. Create your profile! 
2. Start swiping.
3. You’ll start receiving notifications about people liking your profile. Women may receive a huge number of likes, while men may get considerably fewer.
4. Get a match? Don’t wait too long to interact. If you don’t communicate with your match within 24 hours, the match gets archived. Want to restore it? Be prepared to pay.
5. Then come the boosts. If you want more visibility or attention, there are additional paid features encouraging you to spend even more.
6. Here’s where it gets particularly frustrating: after your profile starts getting significant attention, you may suddenly find your account banned for “suspicious activity.”
7. Then you may be asked to provide government-issued identification to prove who you are.
8. Even after submitting legitimate identification, there is no guarantee your account will be restored. You’re left wondering what happens to the sensitive documents you provided in the process.
9. And the appeal process? In my experience, it was incredibly frustrating. You don’t know who is actually reviewing your case, yet a representative can simply tell you that your account is fake — as if they somehow know that with absolute certainty.

The biggest issue isn’t simply that the app costs money. It’s the feeling that you can spend money, build your profile, get engagement, and then potentially

reviews.title: Good concept, terrible execution
reviews.text:
I think it’s great that someone has created a dating app aimed specially at south asian people. It’s a really good concept and could be amazing if the app and its features were refreshed. I will say I personally know a few success stories from DilMil so I did have high hopes.

I don’t like how, despite me setting my filters to suit my preferences, my profile was still shown to men that were way outside of my criteria. For example, I was receiving likes from men who were 15 years older than me, even though I had set my age range only 4 years older than me. This was extremely off putting as these older men were able to message me. I was also being shown to men across the world from me - realistically this would never work and I would have liked to opt out from my profile being shared to men all the way across the planet. I have now deactivated my membership because of this. 

The premium membership is also rubbish. It adds about 3 extra filters and allows you to see the people who have liked you. As I said earlier, this was not useful as the majority of the men who had liked me were WAY outside of the criteria I had set and were rejected immediately. The membership is so crazily overpriced for no reason. I used the 3 day free trial then cancelled before I got charged just so I could see my likes. Please don’t pay for the membership!

reviews.title: Evidence Suggests Dil Mil Discriminates Against Non-Indians
reviews.text: This won’t matter to most users however FYI I am a white guy in LA. I’ve been on the app for over a year. At this point after approximately 18 months on the app I have yet to receive even a single like. Perhaps the girls don’t like me however I have dated multiple Indian and Sri Lankan women who grew up either in the US or overseas so I am skeptical that it’s me. The second bit of evidence is that I have female friends who I have seen on the app multiple times who told me they have never seen me on the app. I asked support if I was shadow-banned and got no response. It is possible they are not bad but merely incompetent however I doubt this. So, I invite other non-Indians on the app to share their experience.
